{{Exclusive|java}} '''Density functions''' make up mathematical expressions to obtain a number from a position, stored as [[JSON]] files within a [[data pack]] in the path data//worldgen/density_function. They are referenced from the [[noise router]] in [[noise settings]]. {{TOC|right}} == JSON format == A density function can be a constant number or an object.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type. ** Other additional fields depend on the value of {{Nbt|string|type}}, described below.
If the {{Nbt|string|type}} is constant, a shorthand format is:
* {{nbt|double}}: A constant number. Value between −1000000.0 and 1000000.0 (both inclusive).
== Marker functions == === {{cd|cache_2d}} === {{until|JE 26.3}} Only computes the input density once per horizontal position.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, cache_2d). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The input to be cached.
=== {{cd|cache_all_in_cell}} === {{until|JE 26.3}} Used by the game onto final_density and should not be referenced in data packs.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, cache_all_in_cell). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The input to be cached.
=== {{cd|cache_once}} === Renamed to {{cd|cache}}.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}} If this density function is referenced twice, it is only computed once per block position.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, cache_once{{until|JE 26.3}} / cache{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|input}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The input to be cached.
=== {{cd|flat_cache}} === {{until|JE 26.3}} Calculate the value per 4×4 column (Value at each block in one column is the same). And it is calculated only once per column, at Y=0. Used often in combination with interpolated.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, flat_cache). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The input to be cached.
=== {{cd|interpolated}} === Interpolates at each block in one cell based on the input density function value of some cells around. The size of each cell is size_horizontal * 4 and size_vertical * 4. Used often in combination with flat_cache.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, interpolated). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|input}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The input to be interpolated. ** {{nbt|int|cell_size_xz}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: Size in blocks of the interpolation grid cells on the X and Z axes. The number must not be negative. ** {{nbt|int|cell_size_y}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: Size in blocks of the interpolation grid cells on the Y axis. The number must not be negative.
== Noise sampling functions == These density functions are used to sample [[Custom noise|noises]]. === {{cd|noise}} === Samples a noise.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, noise). ** {{Nbt|string|noise}}: {{json ref|noise|Custom noise}} — The noise to sample. ** {{Nbt|double|xz_scale}}: Scales the X and Z before sampling. ** {{Nbt|double|y_scale}}: Scales the Y before sampling. ** {{nbt|double|shift_x}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: Optional; A domain warp to apply on X. If not specified, no warping will be applied (equivalent to 0). ** {{nbt|double|shift_y}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: Optional; A domain warp to apply on Y. If not specified, no warping will be applied (equivalent to 0). ** {{nbt|double|shift_z}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: Optional; A domain warp to apply on Z. If not specified, no warping will be applied (equivalent to 0).
=== {{cd|old_blended_noise}} === Samples a legacy noise. {{Info needed}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, old_blended_noise). ** {{Nbt|double|xz_scale}}: Value between 0.001 and 1000.0 (both inclusive). ** {{Nbt|double|y_scale}}: Value between 0.001 and 1000.0 (both inclusive). ** {{Nbt|double|xz_factor}}: Value between 0.001 and 1000.0 (both inclusive). ** {{Nbt|double|y_factor}}: Value between 0.001 and 1000.0 (both inclusive). ** {{Nbt|double|smear_scale_multiplier}}: Value between 1.0 and 8.0 (both inclusive).
=== {{cd|shift}} === Samples a noise at (x/4, y/4, z/4), then multiplies it by 4.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, shift). ** {{Nbt|string|argument}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|string|noise}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref|noise|Custom noise}} — The noise to sample.
=== {{cd|shift_a}} === Samples a noise at (x/4, 0, z/4), then multiplies it by 4.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, shift_a). ** {{Nbt|string|argument}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|string|noise}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref|noise|Custom noise}} — The noise to sample.
=== {{cd|shift_b}} === Samples a noise at (z/4, x/4, 0), then multiplies it by 4.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, shift_b). ** {{Nbt|string|argument}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|string|noise}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref|noise|Custom noise}} — The noise to sample.
=== {{cd|shifted_noise}} === {{until|JE 26.3}} Similar to noise, but first shifts the input coordinates.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, shifted_noise). ** {{Nbt|string|noise}}: {{json ref|noise|Custom noise}} — The noise to sample. ** {{Nbt|double|xz_scale}}: Scales the X and Z before sampling. ** {{Nbt|double|y_scale}}: Scales the Y before sampling. ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|shift_x}}: {{json ref/density function}} — offset of the position in the X direction. ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|shift_y}}: {{json ref/density function}} — offset of the position in the Y direction. ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|shift_z}}: {{json ref/density function}} — offset of the position in the Z direction.
== Mathematical density functions == These density functions are used to perform mathematical operations. === {{cd|abs}} === Calculates the absolute value of the input density function.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, abs). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|input}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The input of the calculation.
=== {{cd|add}} === Adds two density functions together.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, add). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument1}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|left}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The first input of the calculation. ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument2}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|right}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The second input of the calculation.
=== {{cd|ceil}} === Rounds the input value to positive infinity.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, ceil). ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|input}}: Density Function to round. ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|multiple}}: The output will be rounded to an integer multiple of the value returned by this Density Function. If not specified, defaults to a constant 1.
=== {{cd|clamp}} === Clamps the input between two values.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, clamp). ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|input}}: One density function — The input to clamp. ** {{Nbt|double|min}}: The lower bound. Value between −1000000.0 and 1000000.0 (both inclusive). ** {{Nbt|double|max}}: The upper bound. Value between −1000000.0 and 1000000.0 (both inclusive).
=== {{cd|constant}} === A constant value.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, constant). ** {{Nbt|double|argument}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|value}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: A constant value. Value between −1000000.0 and 1000000.0 (both inclusive).
=== {{cd|cube}} === Cubes the input (x^3).
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, cube). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|input}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The input of the calculation.
=== {{cd|div}} === Performs division between two arguments.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, div). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|left}} — The left-hand side of the operation. ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|right}} — The right-hand side of the operation.
=== {{cd|floor}} === Rounds the input value to negative infinity.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, floor). ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|input}}: Density Function to round. ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|multiple}}: The output will be rounded to an integer multiple of the value returned by this Density Function. If not specified, defaults to a constant 1.
=== {{cd|invert}} === Renamed to {{cd|reciprocal}}.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}} Inverts the input (1/x).
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, invert{{until|JE 26.3}} / reciprocal{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The input of the calculation.
=== {{cd|log}} === Computes the natural logarithm of the given input.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, log). ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|input}}: Density Function for which to compute the natural logarithm.
=== {{cd|mul}} === Multiplies two inputs.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, mul). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument1}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|left}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The first input of the calculation. ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument2}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|right}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The second input of the calculation.
=== {{cd|min}} === Returns the minimum of two inputs.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, min). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument1}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|left}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The first input of the calculation. ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument2}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|right}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The second input of the calculation.
=== {{cd|max}} === Returns the maximum of two inputs.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, max). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument1}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|left}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The first input of the calculation. ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument2}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|right}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The second input of the calculation.
=== {{cd|negate}} === Negates the input.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, negate). ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|input}}: Density Function to negate.
=== {{cd|pow}} === Raises the given base value to an exponent.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, pow). ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|base}}: the base value (Density Function). ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|exponent}}: the exponent (Density Function).
=== {{cd|round}} === Rounds the input value to to the nearest integer (ties round up).{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, round). ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|input}}: Density Function to round. ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|multiple}}: The output will be rounded to an integer multiple of the value returned by this Density Function. If not specified, defaults to a constant 1.
=== {{cd|sub}} === Performs subtraction between two arguments.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, sub). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|left}} — The left-hand side of the operation. ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|right}} — The right-hand side of the operation.
=== {{cd|sign}} === Computes the sign of the given input. If positive, it returns as 1. If the input is 0, it returns 0. If negative, it returns as -1.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, sign). ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|input}}: Density Function for which to compute the sign.
=== {{cd|sqrt}} === Computes the square root of the given input.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, sqrt). ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|input}}: Density Function for which to compute the square root.
=== {{cd|square}} === Squares the input. (x^2)
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, square). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|input}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The input of the calculation.
=== {{cd|truncate}} === Rounds the input value to 0.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, truncate). ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|input}}: Density Function to round. ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|multiple}}: The output will be rounded to an integer multiple of the value returned by this Density Function. If not specified, defaults to a constant 1.
== Mapped density functions == These density functions map a set of values onto another set of values. === {{cd|gradient}} === [[File:Gradient tiling.png|thumb|Demonstration of the different tiling options for the {{cd|gradient}} density function{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}, using both an input range of -100 to 100 and an output range of -1 to 1.]] Clamps the given coordinate and maps the gradient to a range.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, gradient). ** {{nbt|string|axis}}: {{cd|x}}, {{cd|y}}. or {{cd|z}}: The axis over which to define the gradient . ** {{nbt|string|tiling}}: How the density function handles values outside the specified coordinate range. 3 options: *** clamp_to_edge: outside the gradient boundaries, the value at the nearest boundary will be used. *** repeat: The gradient will be repeated outside its boundaries. *** mirrored_repeat: The gradient will be repeated as such that odd repetitions are mirrored, ensuring continuity between repetitions. ** {{nbt|int|from_coordinate}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: The coordinate at which the gradient starts. ** {{nbt|int|to_coordinate}}: The coordinate at which the gradient ends. It must not equal {{cd|from_coordinate}}. ** {{nbt|float|from_value}}: The value at which the gradient starts. ** {{nbt|float|to_value}}: The value at which the gradient ends.
=== {{cd|lerp}} === Performs (unclamped) linear interpolation between two arguments based on an alpha.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}} The returned value is: first*(1-alpha) + second*alpha
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, lerp). ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|alpha}}: Density function representing the interpolation factor (e.g. 0 = first, 1 = second). Any value outside of {{cd|[0; 1]}} will extrapolate. ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|first}}: Density Function to use at {{cd|alpha=0}}. ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|second}}: Density Function to use at {{cd|alpha=1}}.
=== {{cd|squeeze}} === First clamps the input between −1 and 1, then transforms it using x/2 - x*x*x/24.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, squeeze). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|input}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The input of the calculation.
=== {{cd|spline}} === Computes a cubic spline.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, spline). ** {{Nbt|float}}{{Nbt|compound|spline}}: The spline. Can be either a number or an object. *** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|coordinate}}: {{json ref/density function}} — Input determining the location on the spline. *** {{Nbt|list|points}}: (Cannot be empty) List of points of the cubic spline. **** {{Nbt|compound}}: A point of the cubic spline. ***** {{Nbt|float|location}}: The location of this point. ***** {{Nbt|float}}{{Nbt|compound|value}}: The value of this point. Can be either a number or a spline object. ***** {{Nbt|float|derivative}}: The slope at this point.
=== {{cd|y_clamped_gradient}} === Replaced with {{cd|gradient}}.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}} Clamps the Y coordinate between from_y and to_y and then linearly maps it to a range.{{until|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, y_clamped_gradient). ** {{Nbt|int|from_y}}: The value to be mapped to from_value. Value between −4064 and 4062 (both inclusive). ** {{Nbt|int|to_y}}: The value to be mapped to to_value. Value between −4064 and 4062 (both inclusive). ** {{Nbt|double|from_value}}: The value to map from_y to. Value between −1000000.0 and 1000000.0 (both inclusive). ** {{Nbt|double|to_value}}: The value to map to_y to. Value between −1000000.0 and 1000000.0 (both inclusive).
== Conditional density functions == These density functions are used to apply "if-then" logic. === {{cd|half_negative}} === If the input is negative, returns half of the input. Otherwise returns the input. (x < 0 ? x/2 : x)
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, half_negative). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|input}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The input of the calculation.
=== {{cd|interval_select}} === Selects between a number of density functions based on an input density function and a set of threshold values.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, interval_select). ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|input}}: Density Function to be compared with any given {{cd|thresholds}}. ** {{nbt|list|thresholds}}: (List of Floats) The threshold values to compare {{cd|input}} with. *** If the input value is less than the threshold values, the result of {{cd|functions[i]}} will be selected. *** If the input value is greater than the last threshold value, the last function will be selected. *** There must be one fewer {{cd|thresholds}} than {{cd|functions}}. ** {{nbt|list|functions}}: The resulting functions (at least two) to be selected from. *** There must be one more element in {{cd|functions}} than {{cd|thresholds}}.
=== {{cd|quarter_negative}} === If the input is negative, returns a quarter of the input. Otherwise returns the input. (x < 0 ? x/4 : x)
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, quarter_negative). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|input}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The input of the calculation.
=== {{cd|range_choice}} === Computes the input value, and depending on that result returns one of two other density functions. Basically an if-then-else statement.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, range_choice). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|input}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The value to compare ** {{Nbt|double|min_inclusive}}: The lower bound of the range. Value between −1000000.0 and 1000000.0 (both inclusive). ** {{Nbt|double|max_exclusive}}: The upper bound of the range. Value between −1000000.0 and 1000000.0 (both inclusive). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|when_in_range}}: {{json ref/density function}} — Used when the input is inside the range. ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|when_out_of_range}}: {{json ref/density function}} — Used when the input is outside the range.
== Other density functions == === {{cd|beardifier}} === Adds beards for structures (see the terrain_adaptation field in [[Structure/JSON format|structures]]). Its value is added to the final_density in noise setting by the game. Should not be referenced in data packs.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, beardifier).
=== {{cd|blend_alpha}} === Used in vanilla for smooth transition to chunks generated in old versions.{{Info needed}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, blend_alpha).
=== {{cd|blend_density}} === Used in vanilla for smooth transition to chunks generated in old versions.{{Info needed}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, blend_density). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument}}{{until|JE 26.3}} / {{nbt|double|input}}{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The desired density of new chunks.
=== {{cd|blend_offset}} === Used in vanilla for smooth transition to chunks generated in old versions.{{Info needed}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, blend_offset).
=== {{cd|distance_to_point}} === [[File:Distance to point options.png|thumb|Demonstration of the different metric options for the {{cd|distance_to_point}} density function{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}, using the distance from the point (0, 0).]] Computes the distance to a fixed point using the specified distance function.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, distance_to_point). ** {{nbt|int-array|point}}: {{cd|[x, y, z]}}; the point to compute distance to ** {{nbt|string|metric}}: *** {{nbt|string|euclidean}}: (i.e. {{cd|sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2)}}) *** {{nbt|string|euclidean_squared}}: (i.e. {{cd|dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2}}) *** {{nbt|string|manhattan}}: (i.e. {{cd|abs(dx) + abs(dy) + abs(dz)}}) *** {{nbt|string|chebyshev}}: (i.e. {{cd|max(abs(dx), abs(dy), abs(dz))}})
=== {{cd|end_islands}} === Renamed to {{cd|end_outer_islands}}.{{upcoming|JE 26.3}} Samples at current position using a noise algorithm used for end islands. Its minimum value is −0.84375 and its maximum value is 0.5625.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, end_islands{{until|JE 26.3}} / end_outer_islands{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}).
=== {{cd|find_top_surface}} === Scans through a column of an input density and returns the topmost y-level that is above 0. If no such position exists within the bounds, the {{Nbt|int|lower_bound}} is returned.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, find_top_surface). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|density}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The density function to scan. ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|upper_bound}}: {{json ref/density function}} — The y-level to start the scan at. Usually a 2D density function. ** {{Nbt|int|lower_bound}}: The y-level to stop the scan. ** {{Nbt|int|cell_height}}: The resolution of the scan. E.g. if set to 4, then only every 4th block is checked.
=== {{cd|ore_vein}} === {{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, ore_vein). ** {{nbt|string|ore_block}}: The ore block to place. ** {{nbt|string|raw_ore_block}}: The raw ore block to place. ** {{nbt|string|filler_block}}: The filler block to place. ** {{nbt|float|raw_ore_chance}}: The probability for a raw ore block to be placed instead of an ore block. Value between 0 and 1 (inclusive). ** {{nbt|int|density}}: The probability for the ore vein to replace a block. If the value is 0 or lower, no block will be replaced. ** {{nbt|int|richness}}: The probability for an ore block or a raw ore block to be placed, as opposed to {{cd|filler_block}}. If the value is 0 or lower, all blocks will be the filler block. If the value is 1 or greater, no blocks will be the filler block. ** {{nbt|int|filler_gap}}: Overrides {{cd|richness}}; if the value is positive, {{cd|filler_block}} will always be placed.
=== {{cd|slice}} === Removes a dimension from the input domain by taking a "slice" along an axis with a specific coordinate (e.g. with the axis equaling y and the coordinate of 0, a slice will be taken along the XZ plane, with all values sampled at y=0).{{upcoming|JE 26.3}}
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, slice). ** {{nbt|string|axis}}: {{cd|x}}, {{cd|y}}, or {{cd|z}}; the axis to remove. ** {{nbt|int|coordinate}}: The fixed coordinate to be passed to the input function. ** {{nbt|string}}{{nbt|double}}{{nbt|compound|input}}: The input function.

* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, slide). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|argument}}: {{json ref/density function}}
=== The legacy "spline" === Removed in [[22w11a]]
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, spline). ** {{Nbt|float}}{{Nbt|compound|spline}}: The spline. Can be either a number or an object. *** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|coordinate}}: {{json ref/density function}} — Input determining the location on the spline. *** {{Nbt|list|points}}: (Cannot be empty) List of points of the cubic spline. **** {{Nbt|float|location}}: The location of this point. **** {{Nbt|float}}{{Nbt|compound|value}}: The value of this point. Can be either a number or a spline object. **** {{Nbt|float|derivative}}: The slope at this point. ** {{Nbt|double|min_value}}: The min value of the output. Value between −1000000.0 and 1000000.0 (both inclusive). ** {{Nbt|double|max_value}}: The max value of the output. Value between −1000000.0 and 1000000.0 (both inclusive).
=== {{cd|terrain_shaper_spline}} === Removed in [[22w11a]] Calculate the spline from the noise settings.
* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, terrain_shaper_spline). ** {{Nbt|string|spline}}: Can be offset, factor, orjaggedness. ** {{Nbt|double|min_value}}: The min value of the output. Value between −1000000.0 and 1000000.0 (both inclusive). ** {{Nbt|double|max_value}}: The max value of the output. Value between −1000000.0 and 1000000.0 (both inclusive). ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|continentalness}}: {{json ref/density function}} ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|erosion}}: {{json ref/density function}} ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|weirdness}}: {{json ref/density function}}

* {{nbt|compound}}: Root object. ** {{Nbt|string|type}}: The ID of the density function type (in this case, weird_scaled_sampler). ** {{Nbt|string|rarity_value_mapper}}: Can be type_1（The minimum scale is 0.75, and the maximum is 2.0）or type_2（The minimum scale is 0.5, and the maximum is 3.0.) ** {{Nbt|string|noise}}: {{json ref|noise|Custom noise}} — The noise to sample. ** {{Nbt|string}}{{Nbt|double}}{{Nbt|compound|input}}: The input density function. Can be an ID of a density function, or a density function in the form of a JSON object or a constant number.
